items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: So, I joined Gus Arnheim's band as the arranger right there.

ctx.x: I said, "Gus Arnheim. Wow." Yeah, Bing Crosby was with him, and, you know, he had the -- he was a great band leader. He says, "She tells me you write music." I said, "Yes, I write it." He says, "Well, do the -- does Earl's band play any of your arrangements?" I said, "Yes." He said, "Well, would you have them to play one or two of them for me when you go back?" I said, "Certainly. I'd be delighted."

So, when I went back, I said, "Hey, Earl." I said, "I have a request to play a couple -- couple of things that I did in the band." Okay, no problem. So, we played them. And, when I went back to the table, he said, "Gee." He says, "I really like those arrangements." He says, "You think you would like to write for my band?" I said, "Sure. I wouldn't mind." He says, "Well, I mean, we're at the Congress Hotel now. We're going to be there for a month." He says, "We got a rehearsal tomorrow morning. Do you think you…
So just bring it on down from there.

Well, I wrote for Gus Arnner and and I wrote for him (inaudible). I wrote for Earl Hines; I wrote for Jerry Jerome as I told you as staff arranger for NBC. I wrote for Billy Eckstein, Sarah Vaughn, and I wrote for Teddy Wilson when he was at CBS with his program. And I wrote for Fletcher Henderson, I wrote for Dizzy Gillespie, I wrote for Woody Herman, I wrote for Gene Krupa, I wrote for Auld George Yorks, I wrote for Ina Rae Hutton, I wrote for Boyd Rabin, and I wrote for Jimmy Noon.
